title: Effort over accomplishment — the just man falls seven times and rises, and the one who gives the new heart says both halves (Proverbs 24; Ezekiel 36; Ephesians 2; Isaiah 46)
summary:
It ain't new. The one who says *I do not this for your sakes* is the same one who says *depart from me, ye that work iniquity*, and the one who promises a new heart is the same one who says that heart will loathe itself for what it did. Both are in the same book, often in the same chapter, and they were never two voices. Proverbs puts the whole of it in one line:

*For a just man falleth seven times, and riseth up again: but the wicked shall fall into mischief.* (Proverbs 24:16)

The just man is not the man who never fell. Nobody is that man:

*For there is not a just man upon earth, that doeth good, and sinneth not.* (Ecclesiastes 7:20)

*If they sin against thee, (for there is no man that sinneth not,) and thou be angry with them, and deliver them to the enemy, so that they carry them away captives unto the land of the enemy, far or near;* (1 Kings 8:46)

*For all have sinned, and come short of the glory of Elohim (God);* (Romans 3:23)

So the line between the just and the wicked is not drawn at the fall. It is drawn at what the man does after it. The just rises. The wicked stops his ears:

*He that turneth away his ear from hearing the law, even his prayer shall be abomination.* (Proverbs 28:9)

*But they refused to hearken, and pulled away the shoulder, and stopped their ears, that they should not hear.* (Zechariah 7:11)

Hear what is done for the house, and for whose sake:

*Therefore say unto the house of Yashar'el (Israel), Thus saith Adonai Yahuah (the Lord GOD); I do not this for your sakes, O house of Yashar'el (Israel), but for mine holy name’s sake, which ye have profaned among the heathen, whither ye went.* (Ezekiel 36:22)

*A new heart also will I give you, and a new spirit will I put within you: and I will take away the stony heart out of your flesh, and I will give you an heart of flesh.* (Ezekiel 36:26)

*And I will put my spirit within you, and cause you to walk in my statutes, and ye shall keep my judgments, and do them.* (Ezekiel 36:27)

And read what the new heart does first, in the very same chapter:

*Then shall ye remember your own evil ways, and your doings that were not good, and shall lothe yourselves in your own sight for your iniquities and for your abominations.* (Ezekiel 36:31)

That is the sign of the new heart: not a head held high because it is saved, and not a head held high because it is righteous, but a head that goes lower the more mercy it sees. Job, Isaiah and Daniel all have it:

*I have heard of thee by the hearing of the ear: but now mine eye seeth thee.* (Job 42:5)

*Wherefore I abhor myself, and repent in dust and ashes.* (Job 42:6)

*Then said I, Woe is me! for I am undone; because I am a man of unclean lips, and I dwell in the midst of a people of unclean lips: for mine eyes have seen the King, Yahuah Tseva'ot (LORD of hosts).* (Isaiah 6:5)

*We have sinned, and have committed iniquity, and have done wickedly, and have rebelled, even by departing from thy precepts and from thy judgments:* (Daniel 9:5)

The one who gives the heart for his own name's sake is the one who also says a name can be blotted out, and that a righteous man who turns away is not carried by what he did before:

*And Yahuah (LORD) said unto Moses, Whosoever hath sinned against me, him will I blot out of my book.* (Exodus 32:33)

*But when the righteous turneth away from his righteousness, and committeth iniquity, and doeth according to all the abominations that the wicked man doeth, shall he live? All his righteousness that he hath done shall not be mentioned: in his trespass that he hath trespassed, and in his sin that he hath sinned, in them shall he die.* (Ezekiel 18:24)

*And then will I profess unto them, I never knew you: depart from me, ye that work iniquity.* (Matthew 7:23)

*He that overcometh, the same shall be clothed in white raiment; and I will not blot out his name out of the book of life, but I will confess his name before my Father, and before his angels.* (Revelation 3:5)

Paul holds both halves in three verses, and the pulpit usually stops reading after the second:

*For by grace are ye saved through faith; and that not of yourselves: it is the gift of Elohim (God):* (Ephesians 2:8)

*Not of works, lest any man should boast.* (Ephesians 2:9)

*For we are his workmanship, created in HaMashiach Yahusha (Christ Jesus) unto good works, which Elohim (God) hath before ordained that we should walk in them.* (Ephesians 2:10)

The gift is for his name's sake, and the walk is the works he ordained. The one who keeps the first half and drops the second has put a period where there was a colon. The one who keeps the second half and drops the first builds a righteousness of the flesh and holds his head up for it. Scripture holds both, because it is one voice. Yahusha (Jesus) sets the measure for a brother at seven times in a day, the proverb's own number:

*And if he trespass against thee seven times in a day, and seven times in a day turn again to thee, saying, I repent; thou shalt forgive him.* (Luke 17:4)

And the whole of it is sealed by the end he declared before any of it began:

*Remember the former things of old: for I am Elohim (God), and there is none else; I am Elohim (God), and there is none like me,* (Isaiah 46:9)

*Declaring the end from the beginning, and from ancient times the things that are not yet done, saying, My counsel shall stand, and I will do all my pleasure:* (Isaiah 46:10)

The end is the gathering: the twelve tribes home, the new heart given, the statutes walked in. The man who falls and rises is on that road. The man who stops his ears has left it, whatever he accomplished. Effort over accomplishment is not a loophole. It is the shape of the whole book.

2421.prose: At Sinai the name can be blotted out of the book. Here the same book comes up again, and the one who overcomes keeps his name in it. The promise only means something because the blotting is real. Yahusha (Jesus) says he will *not blot out his name*, and the warning at the mountain and the promise at the end turn out to be one voice.
2421.phrase: I will not blot out his name out of the book of life
2421.sentence: The name that can be blotted out at Sinai is the name kept for the one who overcomes.

2436.prose: Moses names what the scattered will do: confess their own iniquity and the iniquity of their fathers. Daniel does exactly that. He does not excuse himself or the fathers. He says *we have sinned*, and he measures it against the precepts and judgments, so Torah is still the line he fell from. The fall is named out loud, and the naming is the rising.
2436.phrase: even by departing from thy precepts and from thy judgments
2436.sentence: Daniel confesses the departure from Torah by name, as the law of Moses said the scattered would.

2447.prose: Solomon prays *no man that sinneth not*, and the preacher says the same of the just: there is not one on earth who does good and never sins. Put side by side, they leave no room for a just man who never fell. Nobody is that man, so the line between the just and the wicked has to be drawn somewhere after the fall.
2447.phrase: For there is not a just man upon earth, that doeth good, and sinneth not
2447.sentence: No just man on earth is without sin, so the fall cannot be what divides the just from the wicked.

2432.prose: Job sees Yahuah (LORD) and abhors himself in dust and ashes. Ezekiel says the gathered house will do the same once the new heart is in them: they will remember their ways and *lothe yourselves in your own sight*. Two witnesses, one posture. The head goes down first, and mercy is what lifts it.
2432.phrase: shall lothe yourselves in your own sight for your iniquities and for your abominations
2432.sentence: The new heart's first act is to loathe itself, which is exactly what Job did in the dust.

2449.prose: The psalm's fool says in his heart there is no Elohim (God), and the psalm closes the door on every man: *there is none that doeth good*. Paul writes it down as scripture and says it plainly, none righteous, not one. The verdict on all flesh was old before he wrote it. It is the ground the just man falls on, and what sets him apart is that he rises.
2449.phrase: There is none righteous, no, not one
2449.sentence: Paul quotes the old verdict that no one is righteous, so no man is just by a clean record.

2452.prose: The heavens declare, and Paul says what follows from it: the maker is plainly seen in the things he made, so they are *without excuse*. The witness has been given to every man. The charge is not that men fell. It is what a man does with what he has been shown, and the wicked is the one who turns from it.
2452.phrase: the invisible things of him from the creation of the world are clearly seen
2452.sentence: The witness in creation is given to all, which is why no one can plead that he was never shown.

2442.prose: David asks pardon *for thy name’s sake*, because his iniquity is great. Yahuah (LORD) answers from his own mouth in the same words, *for my name’s sake*, and holds back his anger and does not cut them off. The gift is for the name, not for anything the house earned, and David prays like a man who knows it.
2442.phrase: For my name’s sake will I defer mine anger, and for my praise will I refrain for thee
2442.sentence: Yahuah (LORD) holds back his anger for his own name's sake, which is the ground David prays from.

2410.prose: The proverb says the just man rises. The psalm shows whose hand lifts him. He falls, and he *shall not be utterly cast down*, because Yahuah (LORD) holds him up. The rising is not the man's own strength alone, and the one who holds him is the same one who gave him the new heart.
2410.phrase: he shall not be utterly cast down: for Yahuah (LORD) upholdeth him with his hand
2410.sentence: The just man's rising after the fall is Yahuah (LORD) holding him up with his hand.

2411.prose: Seven falls and he rises. The psalm says who does the raising: Yahuah (LORD) *upholdeth all that fall*, and lifts those who are *bowed down*. The bowed head is not thrown away. It is the very one he lifts, which fits the head that goes lower the more mercy it sees.
2411.phrase: upholdeth all that fall, and raiseth up all those that be bowed down
2411.sentence: Yahuah (LORD) lifts the ones who fall and the ones bowed low, so the fall is not the end.

2412.prose: The new heart is the heart that rises. Adonai Yahuah (the Lord GOD) takes out the *stony heart* and gives *an heart of flesh*, and a heart of flesh is one that can fall, feel it, and get up again. The stopped ear is the stone. Falling is not the verdict. Refusing to rise is.
2412.phrase: I will take away the stony heart out of your flesh, and I will give you an heart of flesh
2412.sentence: The heart of flesh given in place of stone is the heart that rises after it falls.

2409.prose: Micah puts the proverb in the first person: *when I fall, I shall arise*. He sits in darkness and Yahuah (LORD) is his light. He does not claim he never fell, and a verse later he owns that he sinned. What makes him just is that he rises toward the light and does not stop his ears.
2409.phrase: when I fall, I shall arise; when I sit in darkness, Yahuah (LORD) shall be a light unto me
2409.sentence: The prophet speaks the proverb as his own, falling and rising with Yahuah (LORD) as his light.

2413.prose: If the just fall too, here is why. Elohim (God) has *concluded them all in unbelief*, so that he might *have mercy upon all*. Nobody stands on a clean record. The rising comes out of mercy, given for his name's sake, and not out of anything a man accomplished.
2413.phrase: hath concluded them all in unbelief, that he might have mercy upon all
2413.sentence: Everyone is shut up in the fall so that the rising can be mercy and not a wage.

2426.prose: Turn the ear from the law and even the prayer is an abomination. Zechariah shows what that looks like. They made their hearts *an adamant stone*, *lest they should hear the law*. It is the stony heart Ezekiel says gets taken out. The stopped ear and the hard heart are one thing, and the wrath came on those who would not hear.
2426.phrase: they made their hearts as an adamant stone, lest they should hear the law
2426.sentence: The wicked man's stopped ear is a heart made stone on purpose, so that the law is not heard.

2427.prose: Stephen says he sees the Son of Adam standing at the right hand of Elohim (God), and the crowd *stopped their ears* and ran at him. That is the proverb walking about in daylight. The ear is turned from what is said, and the answer to it is violence. The wicked does not fall and rise. He shuts his ears and runs.
2427.phrase: they cried out with a loud voice, and stopped their ears, and ran upon him with one accord
2427.sentence: The crowd that stops its ears at Stephen is the wicked man of the proverb, turning from what he is told.

2448.prose: The preacher says no just man on earth does good and never sins. Paul says it wider: *all have sinned*, and every one falls short of Elohim (God). The fall belongs to everyone, so it cannot be what separates the just from the wicked. The difference has to come after.
2448.phrase: all have sinned, and come short of the glory of Elohim (God)
2448.sentence: Paul widens the preacher's verdict to all, so the fall is common ground and not the dividing line.

2433.prose: Isaiah sees Yahuah (LORD) and cries *woe is me*, undone and unclean. Ezekiel says what the gathered house does under the new heart: *lothe yourselves in your own sight*. It is the same hanging head. The nearer a man gets to the holy one, the lower he goes.
2433.phrase: remember your own evil ways, and your doings that were not good, and shall lothe yourselves in your own sight
2433.sentence: The new heart remembers its own evil ways and loathes itself, the same low cry Isaiah gave before the holy one.

2440.prose: In the earlier chapter the idols are told to *shew the former things* and say what is to come, and they cannot. Here Yahuah (LORD) does it himself: *declaring the end from the beginning*, and his counsel stands. What he named before it happened cannot be turned by any man's effort or failure. The end he named is the gathering.
2440.phrase: the end from the beginning, and from ancient times the things that are not yet done
2440.sentence: Only the one who declares the end from the beginning can answer the challenge, so the end he named stands.

2441.prose: Yahuah (LORD) says *there is none else* and *none like me*. In the earlier chapter he lays down the same claim as a challenge: *produce your cause*, bring your reasons. Anyone who would be Elohim (God) beside him must answer what he has declared. Nobody does, and so his counsel stands.
2441.phrase: bring forth your strong reasons, saith the King of Jacob
2441.sentence: The challenge to bring forth reasons is the other side of his claim that there is none like him.

2438.prose: He declared the end, and he also says he declared the *former things from the beginning*. They went out of his mouth, he did them, and they came to pass. What he spoke, he has done before. So the end he declared will come the same way, and it does not hang on how well the house walked.
2438.phrase: I have declared the former things from the beginning; and they went forth out of my mouth
2438.sentence: What he declared before has already come to pass, which is the record behind the end he declares.

2439.prose: He did the former things as he said he would. Now see where the same voice points: *declaring the end from the beginning*, and *My counsel shall stand*. What he has already done is the pledge of what he has declared. The end stands because the one who said it has kept his word before.
2439.phrase: My counsel shall stand, and I will do all my pleasure
2439.sentence: His counsel stands because what he declared earlier has already come to pass.

2443.prose: Yahuah (LORD) says he holds back his anger for his own name's sake. David asks in the same way, *for thy name’s sake*, and gives his reason: *for it is great*. He does not plead a record. He asks pardon on the name alone. That is the new heart's posture, low and asking.
2443.phrase: For thy name’s sake, O Yahuah (LORD), pardon mine iniquity; for it is great
2443.sentence: David prays the same ground Yahuah (LORD) gave, the name's sake, and brings only his great iniquity.

2419.prose: Ezekiel says that when the righteous turns away and does the abominations, his righteousness *shall not be mentioned*. Yahusha (Jesus) says it again at the end, and those who hear *depart from me* had prophesied and done wonders in his name. Their past works carried nobody. The one who promised the new heart is the one who says it.
2419.phrase: I never knew you: depart from me, ye that work iniquity
2419.sentence: The one who gives the new heart also tells the works of iniquity to depart, as Ezekiel had said.

2437.prose: Ezekiel says it twice. Both times the house remembers its ways and will *lothe yourselves in your own sight*. The hanging head is named once and then named again beside the new heart. It is not a stage the gathered grow out of. It is how they stand before the one who gathered them.
2437.phrase: shall lothe yourselves in your own sight for your iniquities and for your abominations
2437.sentence: The loathing of self is named a second time in Ezekiel, now beside the cleansing and the new heart.

2420.prose: Both verses give the same warning. The righteous who trusts his own righteousness and commits iniquity does not live on what he did before. Here the turning is spelled out: he *doeth according to all the abominations*, and his righteousness is not mentioned. A man's past works do not carry him. The turning does.
2420.phrase: All his righteousness that he hath done shall not be mentioned: in his trespass that he hath trespassed
2420.sentence: The righteous man who turns away loses the standing his earlier righteousness gave him.

2418.prose: His spirit put within them *cause you to walk in my statutes*, and keep his judgments. The proverb shows what that walking looks like. The just man falls seven times and rises. Walking in Torah is not a straight line. It is getting up again. The one who stops his ears stays where he fell.
2418.phrase: a just man falleth seven times, and riseth up again: but the wicked shall fall into mischief
2418.sentence: The walking that the new heart causes includes rising again after the fall, and the wicked does not rise.

2414.prose: Job says it in one line: *I abhor myself*, and he sits in dust and ashes. It is the loathing Ezekiel gives the gathered house. Job had just said his eye now saw Yahuah (LORD), and the sight lowered him. The new heart goes lower the more mercy it sees.
2414.phrase: Wherefore I abhor myself, and repent in dust and ashes
2414.sentence: Job's abhorring of himself in dust and ashes is the same hanging head as loathing yourselves.

2415.prose: Ezekiel says the new heart will loathe itself. Isaiah is that heart in the room. He sees Yahuah (LORD) and does not stand up straighter. He says *Woe is me* and calls himself *undone*. The sight of holiness lowers his head, and the coal that cleans him comes after.
2415.phrase: Woe is me! for I am undone; because I am a man of unclean lips
2415.sentence: Isaiah sees the holy one and loathes himself first, the same lowered head the new heart is promised.

2417.prose: Ezekiel says it twice, so it is no slip of the pen. Gathered out of the countries and brought home, the house of Yashar'el (Israel) will *remember* their ways and loathe themselves. The homecoming does not wipe out the memory. The mercy that brings them back is what lets them see what they were.
2417.phrase: ye shall lothe yourselves in your own sight for all your evils
2417.sentence: Even in the land, even gathered home, the house is told it will loathe itself in its own sight.

2416.prose: Here is the loathing in a man's own mouth. Daniel does not defend himself or his fathers. He piles the words up, *sinned*, *iniquity*, *wickedly*, *rebelled*, and he says *we*, counting himself in. The new heart Ezekiel promises sounds like this prayer.
2416.phrase: We have sinned, and have committed iniquity, and have done wickedly
2416.sentence: Daniel prays the loathing out loud, naming every failure and counting himself among those who failed.

2434.prose: Daniel's prayer is what Leviticus told them to pray. Long before the exile the way back was laid out: confess their own iniquity and *the iniquity of their fathers*. Daniel does exactly that, he and his people together, and the Torah he prays out of has not moved. The confession is the road home, and it was in the law first.
2434.phrase: If they shall confess their iniquity, and the iniquity of their fathers
2434.sentence: Leviticus names confessing the iniquity of the fathers as the way back, and Daniel walks it.

2435.prose: Daniel prays it, Ezekiel promises it. The man on his face in confession is the man Ezekiel describes, who will *remember* his evil ways and *lothe yourselves* before his own eyes. Neither one is boasting of what he has done. The same chapter that promises the heart says the heart will hang its head, and Daniel is already doing it.
2435.phrase: shall lothe yourselves in your own sight for your iniquities
2435.sentence: The promised new heart loathes itself in its own sight, which is what Daniel's confession already sounds like.

2431.prose: Hosea says they were destroyed because they *rejected knowledge* and *forgotten the law*. Proverbs shows what that looks like in one man. He turns his ear away from the law, and even his prayer becomes an abomination. This is the wicked side of the line. He is not marked out by his falling but by the ear he will not give.
2431.phrase: He that turneth away his ear from hearing the law
2431.sentence: The man who turns his ear from the law is the one Hosea says rejected knowledge, and his prayer goes with it.

2428.prose: Zechariah told what the fathers did. They *stopped their ears, that they should not hear*. When Stephen says he sees the Son of Adam standing, his hearers cry out and *stopped their ears* too, then run at him together. The old refusal did not end with the fathers. The ear that will not hear is the sign of the wicked in both places.
2428.phrase: Then they cried out with a loud voice, and stopped their ears
2428.sentence: Stephen's hearers stop their ears the way the fathers did, which is the wicked man's answer to being told.

2429.prose: Zechariah says they made their hearts *an adamant stone* so as not to hear the law. Proverbs gives the cost. The one who turns his ear from the law finds *even his prayer* has become *abomination*. The stone heart is the opposite of the heart of flesh that is promised. It is the wicked man shutting what the just man opens.
2429.phrase: turneth away his ear from hearing the law, even his prayer shall be abomination
2429.sentence: Turning the ear from the law ruins even the prayer, the same refusal Zechariah calls a heart of stone.

2423.prose: Yahusha (Jesus) says it is not the one who says *Adonai* but *he that doeth the will of my Father* who enters. Ezekiel shows what that will is and how it comes to be done. Yahuah (LORD) puts his own spirit within and causes them to walk in his statutes, and they *keep my judgments, and do them*. The gift is what makes the doing possible, and the doing is still asked.
2423.phrase: cause you to walk in my statutes, and ye shall keep my judgments, and do them
2423.sentence: The new heart is given so that the statutes are walked and kept, so the gift and the doing are one promise.

2424.prose: Why would Yahusha (Jesus) say *depart from me* to people who used his name? Ezekiel has already said how it goes. The righteous man who turns away and *committeth iniquity* finds that what he did before does not carry him. A name spoken is not a heart kept, and the ones sent away are the ones *that work iniquity*.
2424.phrase: All his righteousness that he hath done shall not be mentioned
2424.sentence: Righteousness done before the turning away is not counted to the man who turns, which is why he is sent away.

2425.prose: The same Yahusha (Jesus) who says *depart from me* says here *I will not blot out his name*, and he says it to the one who overcomes, clothed in white. So a name can be blotted out and a name can be kept. Those are two sides of one door. The overcomer keeps the walk and the name stays. The one sent away is not confessed before the Father.
2425.phrase: I will not blot out his name out of the book of life
2425.sentence: A name can be blotted from the book of life, and the overcomer's is the one that stays.

2430.prose: Stephen's hearers stopped their ears and ran at him. Zechariah shows where they learned it. The fathers *refused to hearken* and *pulled away the shoulder*, and their children do the same thing with their hands. It is the wicked man's answer, not a fall but a refusal to be told.
2430.phrase: But they refused to hearken, and pulled away the shoulder, and stopped their ears
2430.sentence: The fathers refused to hear and stopped their ears, and Stephen's hearers repeat it exactly.

2454.prose: Elohim (God) *winked at* the times of ignorance, and now he commands every man to repent. Paul in Romans shows why ignorance is no wall to hide behind. What the maker is, his *eternal power*, is *clearly seen* in what he made, *so that they are without excuse*. The call to repent goes to everyone because everyone could see.
2454.phrase: the invisible things of him from the creation of the world are clearly seen
2454.sentence: What can be seen in the creation is why the call to repent leaves no one with an excuse.

2451.prose: Paul says the maker's power is *clearly seen* in what he made. The psalm sang it first. *The heavens declare the glory* of Elohim (God), and the firmament shows his handiwork. Nothing new is added. The sky was already speaking, so the man who stops his ears has nothing to blame but the ears.
2451.phrase: The heavens declare the glory of Elohim (God); and the firmament sheweth his handywork
2451.sentence: The heavens already declare the glory of Elohim (God), which is the witness Paul says leaves men without excuse.

2453.prose: Paul sees *the work of the law written in their hearts*. Jeremiah says where that writing comes from and whose law it is. Yahuah (LORD) tells the house of Yashar'el (Israel) that he will *put my law in their inward parts*. It is the same law, Torah, not a new one, and the new covenant is that law on the heart. What Paul sees at work is what Jeremiah promised.
2453.phrase: I will put my law in their inward parts, and write it in their hearts
2453.sentence: The new covenant is the law itself written on the heart, which is what Paul sees working inside.

2444.prose: Paul writes *There is none righteous* and says *as it is written*. This is where. The psalm says the fool's heart says there is no Elohim (God), and then *there is none that doeth good*. It puts every man on the same ground before anyone can boast, which is why the line between just and wicked cannot be drawn at the fall.
2444.phrase: They are corrupt, they have done abominable works, there is none that doeth good
2444.sentence: The psalm levels every man on the same ground, so the just are not the ones who never fell.

2445.prose: Paul's *all have sinned* is no new charge. Solomon said it at the dedication of the house: *there is no man that sinneth not*. He said it as the ground for asking mercy, because a people that sin will be carried away captive, and a people that bethink themselves and repent can come home. The fall is expected. What follows it is what counts.
2445.phrase: for there is no man that sinneth not
2445.sentence: Solomon names the universal sin as the ground for repenting and coming home, long before Paul.

2446.prose: Two letters, one sentence. Romans says Elohim (God) *concluded them all in unbelief*, and Galatians says the scripture *concluded all under sin*. Both shut the door on boasting and open it on mercy and the promise. Galatians does not set the law against the promises either. The verse just before asks that very thing and answers no.
2446.phrase: the scripture hath concluded all under sin, that the promise by faith of Yahusha HaMashiach (Jesus Christ) might be given
2446.sentence: Everyone is shut up under sin so that the promise is given as mercy, not earned as a wage.

2455.prose: James says faith with no works is *dead, being alone*. Here is what that looks like. The ones Yahusha (Jesus) sends away have used his name, prophesied and cast out devils, and he still says *I never knew you*. A name spoken with no walk behind it is a dead thing. They *work iniquity*, and the Torah that iniquity breaks is still standing.
2455.phrase: I never knew you: depart from me, ye that work iniquity
2455.sentence: Those who claimed the name yet worked iniquity are the dead faith James describes, and they are sent away.

2456.prose: James says faith without works is dead, like a body without the spirit. The proverb shows what living faith does. It falls and *riseth up again*. Not the man who never fell, but the one who gets up. The wicked man *shall fall into mischief* and stay there. The works James asks for are the rising.
2456.phrase: For a just man falleth seven times, and riseth up again
2456.sentence: Living faith is the just man's rising after each fall, and dead faith is the one that stays down.

2450.prose: John says the man who claims to have *no sin* only *deceive ourselves*. Paul gives the reason, *all have sinned*, and adds that they *come short of the glory*. So the man who denies the fall is lying to himself. The just man is the one who admits it and rises. Nobody has a record clean enough to hold his head up on.
2450.phrase: For all have sinned, and come short of the glory of Elohim (God)
2450.sentence: Everyone has sinned, so denying it is self deceit and the only honest road is confession and rising.

2422.prose: Yahusha (Jesus) says *I will not blot out his name*, and he speaks in the light of Sinai. Yahuah (LORD) told Moses that whoever sinned against him he would *blot out of my book*. So the book is real and names can come off it. The overcomer's name stays. It is the old law of the book, not a new one, that the promise leans on.
2422.phrase: Whosoever hath sinned against me, him will I blot out of my book
2422.sentence: Sinai already says names are blotted out of the book, which is why keeping the name is a promise to the overcomer.

2515.prose: The speaker wishes it had been better *not to have given the earth to Adam*, because Adam could not be held back from sinning. Paul puts the verdict plainly: *There is none righteous, no, not one*. Both come to the same place. No one stands before the Father on a clean record, and that is where the just man's rising begins.
2515.phrase: There is none righteous, no, not one
2515.sentence: Paul states the universal verdict plainly, the same one the speaker reaches by grieving over Adam.

7071.prose: Yahusha (Jesus) tells us to rebuke a brother who trespasses, and *if he repent, forgive him*. The proverb shows who that brother is. A *just man* falls and *riseth up again*. Repentance is the rising. The same voice gives the proverb and the forgiveness, and the next line sets the number at seven times in a day, the proverb's own number.
7071.phrase: For a just man falleth seven times, and riseth up again
7071.sentence: The forgiven brother is the just man of the proverb, who falls and rises by repenting.

5041.prose: Yahusha (Jesus) says *Take heed what ye hear*, and *unto you that hear shall more be given*. The proverb is that hearing played out in a life. The just man falls and still listens, so he rises. The wicked man falls and does not. More is given to the ear that stays open.
5041.phrase: For a just man falleth seven times, and riseth up again
5041.sentence: The just man's rising is hearing carried through a fall, and more is given to the one who hears.

2514.prose: The writer says there is none born who has not *dealt wickedly*, and not even among the faithful is there one *which has not done amiss*. Paul puts it in one line, *all have sinned*, and adds *come short of the glory*. Same verdict. It levels everyone before the rising begins.
2514.phrase: For all have sinned, and come short of the glory of Elohim (God)
2514.sentence: The universal verdict that all have sinned is the baseline the just man's rising starts from.

5148.prose: Whoever clings to his life loses it, and whoever lets it go for the sake of Yahusha (Jesus) keeps it. The proverb walks the same road from the other end. The just man is knocked down and *riseth up again*. The wicked is the one who will not get up, and he *shall fall into mischief*.
5148.phrase: a just man falleth seven times, and riseth up again
5148.sentence: Seven falls do not end the just man because he rises each time, and that is losing a life in order to keep it.

2517.prose: Both verses shut the same door. The maker was plain from what he made, so the ones who looked past him are *without excuse*. The fault is not that no witness stood in sight. The fault is ears that would not turn to it, and that is the wicked, not the just man who falls and rises.
2517.phrase: so that they are without excuse
2517.sentence: Being without excuse belongs to those who had the witness in plain sight and would not hear it.

5149.prose: Same saying, said again in Matthew. The man who *findeth his life* by holding on to it loses it, and the one who gives it up for the sake of Yahusha (Jesus) *shall find it*. The loss is not in falling. The loss is in clinging to self.
5149.phrase: he that loseth his life for my sake shall find it
5149.sentence: Losing the life for his sake is how it is found, which is the head that goes low and then rises.

2516.prose: If men could measure so much of the world, the maker should not have been hard to find. Paul says the same plainly: what he made shows *his eternal power*, and nobody stands without a witness. Ears that hear find him. Ears stopped leave a man with no defense.
2516.phrase: the invisible things of him from the creation of the world are clearly seen
2516.sentence: The maker is plain from what he made, so those who still miss him do it with stopped ears, not for want of a witness.

5150.prose: John gives the same word a harder edge: *hateth his life in this world*. This is the man who stops grabbing for himself, whose head goes lower the more mercy he sees. He is not despising a gift. He is the one who *shall keep it unto life eternal*.
5150.phrase: he that hateth his life in this world shall keep it unto life eternal
5150.sentence: Hating the life that clings to itself is the lowered head, and the end of that road is life eternal.

2518.prose: Nobody gets to look down on a man who turns back from sin, because the same verdict sits on everyone. Paul says it flat: all have *come short*. The line between men is not drawn at the fall. It is drawn at whether a man turns, and neither writer leaves room to sneer.
2518.phrase: For all have sinned, and come short of the glory of Elohim (God)
2518.sentence: Everyone has come short, so what separates men is what they do after the fall, not whether they fell.

5153.prose: The man who gains the world has nothing to buy his soul back with. Those who trust their wealth cannot *by any means redeem his brother*, and no ransom is theirs to hand to Elohim (God). What a man piled up does not count. What he does with his heart does.
5153.phrase: None of them can by any means redeem his brother, nor give to Elohim (God) a ransom for him
5153.sentence: No pile of wealth buys a soul back, so the gain of the whole world answers nothing.

2519.prose: Both prayers put righteousness on one side and shame on the other. Daniel spreads it over *all Yashar'el (Israel)*, near and far, scattered through the countries where they were driven. The shame is owned and not argued away. That is the head going lower, not the ears stopping.
2519.phrase: righteousness belongeth unto thee, but unto us confusion of faces, as at this day
2519.sentence: Righteousness is his and the confusion of faces is ours, the loathing of the new heart said aloud.

5151.prose: Matthew keeps the question and adds a second one. A man who has gained the whole world is asked what he will *give in exchange for his soul*. Nothing he built can be laid on the counter. So the just man's rising is no payment. It is a heart that turns and gets up.
5151.phrase: what shall a man give in exchange for his soul?
5151.sentence: Nothing a man has gained can be traded for his soul, so accomplishment cannot be the price.

2521.prose: A knee that bows in the heart and begs for grace is the new heart Ezekiel names. It remembers *your own evil ways* and does not argue. The prayer asks, and the promise says what the heart will do once it is given. Mercy and loathing arrive together.
2521.phrase: shall lothe yourselves in your own sight for your iniquities and for your abominations
2521.sentence: The new heart's first act is to remember its own ways and loathe itself, which is the bowed knee in a promise.

5152.prose: Luke ends the question differently: a man may *lose himself, or be cast away*. The one who gains everything and loses himself is the one who never turned. Falling does not do that to a man. Refusing to rise does.
5152.phrase: if he gain the whole world, and lose himself, or be cast away?
5152.sentence: The loss named here is the man himself, which comes from refusing to turn, not from the falls along the way.

2520.prose: Both prayers confess in the first person and hold nothing back. Daniel's cry, *We have sinned*, is a whole people on its knees, and the other prayer says *I have sinned* for one man. Neither pleads that it did enough. That is the loathing of the new heart, in words.
2520.phrase: even by departing from thy precepts and from thy judgments
2520.sentence: The confession names the departure from precepts and judgments and pleads no accomplishment, only the turning back.

5178.prose: The father cries out *I believe; help thou mine unbelief* with tears, and he is not turned away. He is the just man in the middle of a fall, and he is already on his way up because he cries. A man who *falleth seven times* and cries out is not the wicked, who stops his ears.
5178.phrase: a just man falleth seven times, and riseth up again
5178.sentence: A half believing man who cries for help is the just man mid fall, already rising.

2522.prose: The end was named before the road began, and it is a good end: *My counsel shall stand*. The righteous in Enoch finish their days in peace, and Isaiah says the one who declared *the end from the beginning* has already settled it. The gathering is not in doubt, so the man who falls and rises is walking toward it.
2522.phrase: saying, My counsel shall stand, and I will do all my pleasure
2522.sentence: His counsel stands, so the end he declared, the gathering home, will come, and the one who rises is on that road.

5179.prose: The father has no steady faith to offer, only a cry. The answer was written long before: *I will help thee*, from the one who is *thy Elohim (God)*. The man who stumbles is not told to be clean first. He is told not to fear, because he will be held up.
5179.phrase: I will strengthen thee; yea, I will help thee; yea, I will uphold thee
5179.sentence: The help does not wait on a clean record, because the one who speaks promises to strengthen and uphold.

5202.prose: Yahusha (Jesus) looked at the man and loved him, and then named one thing he lacked. What he asked was a step, not more accomplishment to count. The proverb says the just man *riseth up again*, so the road is the next step after coming short, taken in love.
5202.phrase: falleth seven times, and riseth up again: but the wicked shall fall into mischief
5202.sentence: The next step after coming short is what the proverb counts, not a record of what was achieved.

5228.prose: *Have faith in Elohim (God)* is trust that keeps walking, not a formula. The just man's trust is that he gets up after a fall, seven times over, because he looks to the one who sets him on his feet. The wicked stop their ears and call the fall the end.
5228.phrase: falleth seven times, and riseth up again
5228.sentence: Faith in Elohim (God) is what gets the just man up again after each fall.

5229.prose: To have faith in Elohim (God) is to hear him say *Fear thou not; for I am with thee*. The faith rests on what he says he will do, not on a clean record. The man held up is a man who has stumbled, and the hand holding him is *the right hand of my righteousness*, not his own.
5229.phrase: I will uphold thee with the right hand of my righteousness
5229.sentence: Faith rests on his hand holding the stumbling man up, not on the man's own righteousness.

5258.prose: Yahusha (Jesus) sits and watches the money go in, and *many that were rich* put in much. Samuel is told the same measure long before: man looks at the outside, but Yahuah (LORD) looks at the heart. The heart behind the offering is weighed, not the size of the pile.
5258.phrase: man looketh on the outward appearance, but Yahuah (LORD) looketh on the heart
5258.sentence: He weighs the heart behind the gift, so a large pile proves nothing and a small one can be the more.

5257.prose: The rich *cast in much* and it counts for little. The proverb sets the measure at the rising, not at the pile. A man who falls seven times and gets up has given more of himself than a full hand of coin that never touched the heart.
5257.phrase: a just man falleth seven times, and riseth up again
5257.sentence: The measure is the getting up after falling, not the size of what was given or gained.

5332.prose: Peter is down in the palace and a maid of the high priest is coming for him. He is about to fall, and badly. The proverb says the just man falls and *riseth up again*, so the failure does not cancel the calling. What counts is whether he gets up.
5332.phrase: For a just man falleth seven times, and riseth up again
5332.sentence: Peter's coming fall is the kind the just man rises from, so it does not annul his calling.

5333.prose: Peter denied him down in the high priest's palace, and here Yahusha (Jesus) asks him *lovest thou me more than these*. He is not thrown out. He is given lambs to feed. The man who fell is the man sent to work.
5333.phrase: Simon, son of Jonah, lovest thou me more than these?
5333.sentence: The fallen man is asked about love and handed lambs, which is the rising after the fall.

5368.prose: The word is sent to *his disciples and Peter*, and Peter is named out loud. The one who fell is singled out to hear that Yahusha (Jesus) is going ahead and will be seen. That is the proverb at work: the just man falls and *riseth up again*.
5368.phrase: For a just man falleth seven times, and riseth up again
5368.sentence: Naming Peter in the message sends the restoring word to the one who fell, so he can rise.

5369.prose: Peter was named in the word the women carried, and when Yahusha (Jesus) meets him he asks only *lovest thou me*. Then comes *Feed my lambs*. The man who denied him is sent back to work, not struck off the list.
5369.phrase: thou knowest that I love thee. He saith unto him, Feed my lambs.
5369.sentence: The denier is answered with a commission, so the word sent to Peter by name is kept.

5374.prose: He upbraided the eleven for *unbelief and hardness of heart*, and the next thing he does is give work. At the table with Peter he asks *lovest thou me* and answers with the call to feed. Rebuke and commission come together from the same Yahusha (Jesus).
5374.phrase: So when they had dined, Yahusha (Jesus) saith to Simon Peter
5374.sentence: The scolded disciples are the ones he still feeds and sends, so the rebuke and the commission are one motion.
